title: Building/sending the upstream CONNECT and forming the authority
answers: How is the CONNECT request to the upstream proxy built?
How is the CONNECT authority formed?
How to add Proxy-Authorization to upstream CONNECT?
How is the upstream CONNECT response handled?
body:
`layers/http/_upstream_proxy.py:HttpUpstreamProxy` subclasses `tunnel.TunnelLayer` (conn=ctx.server target, tunnel_connection=proxy Server created in `HttpUpstreamProxy.make` from `ctx.server.via`; for https proxy first pushes `tls.ServerTLSLayer` with alpn `HTTP1_ALPNS`, sni=proxy host).
- `start_handshake`: if not send_connect -> `TunnelLayer.start_handshake` (no CONNECT). Else builds `http.HTTPFlow(client, tunnel_connection)` with `http.Request` method CONNECT, scheme/path empty, HTTP/1.1, host/port from conn.address; optional `Host` header first if option `http_connect_send_host_header`; yields `HttpConnectUpstreamHook(flow)` (addon hook to edit, e.g. Proxy-Authorization); serialises with `http1.assemble_request` and `commands.SendData(tunnel_connection, raw)`.
- Authority: `self.conn.address[0].encode("idna") + f":{port}".encode()` — IDNA host, port always appended, no IPv6 brackets.
- `receive_handshake_data`: buffers in h11 ReceiveBuffer until head complete, `http1.read_response_head`; 2xx -> (True, None) and leftover bytes re-fed; non-2xx/parse error -> (False, "Upstream proxy ... refused HTTP CONNECT request"); incomplete -> (False, None).
